entity.name: Clarvia ASBL
entity.description: Clarvia ASBL is a Luxembourg-registered nonprofit developing free, source-backed global guidance and open public-interest infrastructure for navigating complex administrative processes after a terminal illness diagnosis or the death of a loved one. Clarvia combines Ask Clarvia (live source-cited email answers), a 1,000-page multilingual guidance library across 196 countries and 200 cross-border corridors in 14 languages, an interactive bereavement checklist, open schemas, validation tooling, and a normalized legislation corpus. Founded by two unpaid co-founders and supported by core staff (1 FTE) and open-source contributors, Clarvia develops its work in collaboration with public authorities, nonprofit organisations, and community contributors.

projects.name: Clarvia Graph
projects.description:
Clarvia Graph is an open, source-backed knowledge graph, global guidance corpus, and toolchain for modelling administrative consequences after major life events (terminal illness and bereavement). It structures official rules, conditions, deadlines, required documents, responsible authorities, and source evidence so that families, public services, nonprofit organisations, civic-technology projects, and researchers can access and reuse trustworthy administrative workflows.

The monorepo powers clarvia.org — including Ask Clarvia (source-cited email guidance), a 1,000-page multilingual guidance library covering 592 guides across all 196 countries and 200 cross-border corridors in 14 languages, an interactive bereavement checklist launched first in Luxembourg, and the normalized legislation corpus (lex/). Every published claim is designed to trace to an authoritative source. The project includes open schemas, controlled vocabularies, graph data, source registries, 9-layer graph CI validation and 4-layer guidance factual verification tooling, automated tests, and JSON exports (with JSON-LD EU interoperability views planned).

Funding is sought to expand formal Clarvia Graph and normalized legislation (lex/) coverage across jurisdictions, deepen expert legal and institutional review, and sustain long-term public-interest operations.

channels.description: Bank-transfer details for Clarvia ASBL are published on this page. Institutional funders may contact opensource@clarvia.org for due-diligence and transfer documentation.

plans.name: Clarvia Graph adoption-ready first release
plans.description: One-time funding to prepare Clarvia Graph for independent evaluation and reuse. The work will produce a stable versioned release, improved installation and contributor documentation, reproducible examples, stronger validation and automated testing, public governance and roadmap documentation, and an independent technical review.

plans.name: General open-source support
plans.description: Flexible contributions supporting maintenance, documentation, source validation, community participation, infrastructure, and continued development of Clarvia Graph.
